investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: Yes, can I help you?

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.player: Queen Sigrid tells me that things have been going missing from the kingdom. Can you tell me anything about this?

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Helga
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: You're the regent of Miscellania, aren't you?

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Helga
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: I'm surprised you didn't know about your own soldiers demanding tribute from us.

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Helga
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: I told them to go away, but the next day I found that they'd stolen my small shield!

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Helga
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: How am I supposed to defend the house without it?

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Helga
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: And what am I going to use as a fruit bowl in the meantime?

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Helga
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: Please sort out your soldiers, and get my shield back to me.

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.player: I'll see what I can do.
Excuse me...

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Ashild
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: What is it?

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.player: Queen Sigrid tells me that things have been going missing from the kingdom. Can you tell me anything about this?

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Ashild
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: Curse those Miscellanian soldiers!

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Ashild
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: They came and demanded tribute, and even though I told them to go away, they came back at night and stole my farming tools!

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Ashild
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: Without my trowel and fork, I can't do anything to keep the weeds from the farming patch.

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Ashild
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: Please, find my tools again, so I can get back to work.

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.player: I'll see what I can do.
Excuse me...

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Moldof
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: What is it?

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.player: Queen Sigrid tells me that things have been going missing from the kingdom. Can you tell me anything about this?

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Moldof
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: You didn't know about it?

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Moldof
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: Miscellanian soldiers came here a few days ago, saying they wanted us to pay tribute.

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Moldof
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: Of course, I told them to leave.

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Moldof
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: But in the morning, I found they'd stolen my quiver of arrows!

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Moldof
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: They're not very valuable arrows, but I need them to do my job. Could you get them back for me?

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.player: I'll see what I can do.
Excuse me...

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Arnor
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: Yes, what is it?

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.player: Queen Sigrid tells me that things have been going missing from the kingdom. Can you tell me anything about this?

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Arnor
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: You mean you haven't heard?

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Arnor
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: Only a few days ago, we had Miscellanian soldiers come round and ask for tribute.

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Arnor
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: I told them to get lost, of course...

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Arnor
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: ...but when I woke up the next morning, they'd stolen my sword!

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Arnor
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: Could you get it back for me? I doubt it can cut anything, but it once belonged to my great-grandfather.

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Arnor
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: So it's a family heirloom, you see.

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.player: I'll see what I can do.

investigating-the-stolen-goods-returning.speaker: Queen Sigrid
investigating-the-stolen-goods-returning.text: Have you talked to the citizens yet, [Fremennik name]?

investigating-the-stolen-goods-returning.player: I've talked to the Miscellanian citizens as well as the Etceterians.
The Etceterian citizens said that Miscellanian soldiers came to their houses and demanded tribute...

investigating-the-stolen-goods-returning.speaker: Queen Sigrid
investigating-the-stolen-goods-returning.text: Just as I suspected! Vargas, you treacherous snake!

investigating-the-stolen-goods-returning.player: ...and the Miscellanian citizens said that the Etceterian army marched into their fields and demanded tithes!

investigating-the-stolen-goods-returning.speaker: Queen Sigrid
investigating-the-stolen-goods-returning.text: Now I see his plan! Vargas isn't content with simply arguing; he wants to start a war even if it means swindling his own citizens!

investigating-the-stolen-goods-returning.speaker: Queen Sigrid
investigating-the-stolen-goods-returning.text: Etceterian army? There hasn't been one for centuries! These Miscellanian soldiers of his must have disguised themselves.

investigating-the-stolen-goods-returning.speaker: Queen Sigrid
investigating-the-stolen-goods-returning.text: And since Vargas shouldn't even be ruling now, it's your responsibility to deal with this.

investigating-the-stolen-goods-returning.speaker: Queen Sigrid
investigating-the-stolen-goods-returning.text: The one who should sort this out is you.

options.text: I suppose so...

steps.player: I suppose you're right.

options.text: Me?

steps.player: Me?

steps.speaker: Queen Sigrid
steps.text: It's one of the hazards of ruling a country, [Fremennik name].

steps.player: I suppose you're right.

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Queen Sigrid
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: Have you found those stolen items yet?

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.player: Not yet, your Majesty.

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Queen Sigrid
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: You'd better hurry and look for them.

investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.speaker: Queen Sigrid
investigating-the-stolen-goods-talking-t.text: We don't know what Vargas might be planning next!

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.text: Have you spoken to the citizens yet, [Fremennik name]?

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.player: I've spoken to the Miscellanian citizens, and also the Etceterians.
The Miscellanian citizens said that the Etceterian army marched into their fields and demanded tithes...

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.text: I see. Sigrid thinks that now I've recognised Etceteria as a sovereign nation, I'll just roll over and play dead when she tries to invade, does she?

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.player: ...and the Etceterian citizens said that Miscellanian soldiers came to their houses and demanded tribute!

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.text: And she's even started spreading rumours among her own citizens! Are there no depths to which she won't sink?

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.text: Lying to her own people about there being Miscellanian soldiers... we don't even have an army!

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.text: Which makes it all the worse, as otherwise I'd be able to invade Etceteria to save the citizens from Sigrid's depravity.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.player: I'm not sure that would work very well, your Majesty.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.text: In any case, if there are any 'Miscellanian soldiers', they must have come from somewhere.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.text: Ask Advisor Ghrim if he knows who they might be, or where they might have come from.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.text: He's a capable advisor, so I'm sure he'll know about any suspicious people.

options.text: King Vargas asked me to talk to you.

steps.player: King Vargas asked me to talk to you.
He said you might know more about the missing goods.

steps.speaker: Advisor Ghrim
steps.text: I'm not sure what you're implying, Your Royal Highness.

steps.player: Er... that you could advise me where to look for them?

steps.speaker: Advisor Ghrim
steps.text: Ah, of course.

steps.speaker: Advisor Ghrim
steps.text: Assuming that nobody presently living in Miscellania would have taken them,

steps.speaker: Advisor Ghrim
steps.text: it is of course likely that someone from outside took them.

steps.speaker: Advisor Ghrim
steps.text: The sailor who brought you here from the mainland would be the first to see any suspicious visitors.

steps.speaker: Advisor Ghrim
steps.text: I suggest you ask him about recent arrivals to the island.

options.text: How is the Kingdom faring?
How do I manage the kingdom?
What am I meant to be doing again?

steps.player: What am I meant to be doing again?

steps.speaker: Advisor Ghrim
steps.text: ...I believe the King asked you to talk to me, Your Royal Highness.

steps.player: Yes, that's right.

options.text: Hello. Can I get a ride on your ship?
I'm looking for a sailor...

steps.player: I'm looking for a sailor...

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: You've found one here. Can I help you?

steps.player: The King's advisor said I should talk to you. He said there have been some suspicious people arriving recently.

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: Well, I don't know of any suspicious people... Advisor Ghrim can be rather paranoid about these things sometimes.

steps.player: Oh. Has anyone visited the island recently, then?

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: Nobody apart from you, and those kids from Rellekka.

steps.player: What kids from Rellekka?

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: Five of them came over here a few weeks ago. They said they were here to see relatives in the dungeons, and they were visiting from the mainland.

steps.player: I didn't realise the King kept people in his dungeons.
I didn't know Miscellania even HAD dungeons.

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: They've not been used to keep prisoners for a long time. But since the war ended, we've had more people visiting the island.

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: Some of them decided they wanted to stay, so we've had to find somewhere for them to live...

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: Only the weather on Miscellania is terrible, and nobody could build houses that would stand up to a strong wind. Etceteria is just the same.

steps.player: So you decided to live in the dungeons instead?

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: Well, of course, they had to be enlarged first. There are still some dwarves working there, making more of the dungeons inhabitable before they move over to work in Etceteria.

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: If you're looking for those kids from Rellekka, you'll find them in those dungeons.

steps.speaker: Sailor
steps.text: Why are you surprised about this, though? I thought you'd become the Regent.

steps.player: I'm still an adventurer, and I can't be everywhere in Gielinor...

to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.text: Sorry, but nobody's allowed down there by order of the King.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.player: But I'm the Regent! I order you to let me go down there.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.text: You're the Regent? Well, I didn't vote for you.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.text: Sorry, 'Regent', nobody can go into the dungeons without the King's say-so.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.player: What'll it take to convince you that I'm really the Regent?

to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.text: If the King came and told me, then I'd believe it.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.text: Or, if he can't come here himself, I suppose a royal proclamation would be fine.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.player: Does he have to shout it from the battlements, or something like that?

to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-attempting-to-en.text: No, just his signature and a statement saying you're really the Regent would do.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.player: Your Majesty, how do I get into the dungeons?

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.text: Of course, how could I have forgotten?

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.text: I'm surprised I didn't tell you when you were appointed Regent.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.player: It's okay, the sailor explained it to me.
He said that the only new arrivals on the island were some teenagers, who came from Rellekka to visit their relatives.
Those relatives were living in the houses in the dungeons.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.text: Ah, so you wish to look in the dungeons in case these new arrivals are to blame?

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.text: I doubt that anyone with Miscellanian relatives would be at fault. However...

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.text: There is something I need you to do in the dungeons.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.text: They are still being excavated, and the dwarven architects are finding new caves as they go. There have been reports of odd sightings in these new caves.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.text: Perhaps they are monsters, waiting to devour unwary Miscellanians...

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.text: Whatever they are, I want you to look into it.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.text: You are a member of the royal family, after all, so I know I can rely on your help.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.text: The guard by the dungeon entrance may not recognise you, since he was only hired recently. Here, take this scroll to show that you have access to the dungeons.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-asking-king-varg.text: You'll find the entrance by the south-east corner of the palace.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.speaker: King Vargas
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.text: Have you given that scroll to the guard yet?
If the player still has the scroll:

steps.player: Not yet, your Majesty.

steps.text: (Continues with Changing heirs dialogue.)

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-king-.text: If the player lost the scroll:

steps.player: I seem to have lost it.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: Honestly... very well, I'll write you another one.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: Try not to lose it this time.
(Continues with Changing heirs dialogue.)

options.text: How is the Kingdom faring?
How do I manage the kingdom?
What am I meant to be doing again?

steps.player: What am I meant to be doing again?

steps.speaker: Advisor Ghrim
steps.text: Showing the dungeon guard that you have permission to enter, Your Royal Highness.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.text: Sorry, but nobody's allowed down there by order of the King.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.player: But I'm the Regent! I order you to let me go down there.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.text: You're the Regent? Well, I didn't vote for you.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.text: Sorry, 'Regent', nobody can go into the dungeons without the King's say-so.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.player: Look, the King gave me a scroll saying I have access to the dungeons. I have it right here.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.text: Hmm... all seems to be in order.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.text: All right, your Highness, you're free to go down there.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.speaker: Guard
to-the-dungeon-with-you-entering-the-dun.text: Try not to be eaten by monsters.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-halla.speaker: Halla
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-halla.text: Welcome to Miscellania's first clothing store! We sell clothing made especially for Fremenniks and Dwarves.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-halla.speaker: Halla
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-halla.text: Can I help you with anything, Your Royal Highness?

options.text: I'd like to look at what you have for sale.
No thank you, I'm fine.
What's it like living down here?

steps.player: What's it like living down here?

steps.speaker: Halla
steps.text: It's very spacious. One of the dwarves said that the caves go on for miles!

steps.speaker: Halla
steps.text: I don't like these rumours I've heard about the other caves, though.

steps.player: What rumours?

steps.speaker: Halla
steps.text: They say there might be monsters in there. You'd best talk to the dwarves who are excavating - they'd know about these stories.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-osval.speaker: Osvald
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-osval.text: Welcome to the Miscellania food store. We've only opened recently.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-osval.speaker: Osvald
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-osval.text: Would you like to buy anything, your Royal Highness?

options.text: Could you show me what you have for sale?
No thank you, I don't need food just now.
What's it like living down here?

steps.player: What's it like living down here?

steps.speaker: Osvald
steps.text: The town's growing larger, and business is doing well.

steps.speaker: Osvald
steps.text: I'm worried about the stories I've heard about monsters, though.

steps.player: What stories about monsters?

steps.speaker: Osvald
steps.text: I heard that one of the dwarves saw monsters in the other caves!

steps.speaker: Osvald
steps.text: I don't know more than that, so you'd have to ask the dwarves.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-finn.speaker: Finn
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-finn.text: Can I help you, your Royal Highness?

options.text: Yes please. What are you selling?
No thanks.
What's it like living down here?

steps.player: What's it like living down here?

steps.speaker: Finn
steps.text: There's no rain or wind down here.

steps.speaker: Finn
steps.text: Some of the dwarves say that there's water in the other caves, and one of them says he's seen monsters in there.

steps.player: Monsters? What sort of monsters?

steps.speaker: Finn
steps.text: I don't know, sorry. You'd better ask one of the dwarves about it.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-runa.speaker: Runa
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-runa.text: Would you like to try some fine Miscellanian ale, Your Royal Highness?

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-runa.speaker: Runa
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-runa.text: Well, I say Miscellanian, but it's actually brewed on the mainland.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-runa.speaker: Runa
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-runa.text: Would you like to try some anyway?

options.text: Yes, please.
No, thank you.
What's it like living down here?

steps.player: What's it like living down here?

steps.speaker: Runa
steps.text: The dwarves living down here spend a lot of time and money in my inn.

steps.speaker: Runa
steps.text: One of them's been in here all day, and only bought one pint.

steps.speaker: Runa
steps.text: Could you ask him to at least order another drink?

steps.player: I'll see what I can do.

options.text: What are you doing down here?

steps.player: What are you doing down here?

steps.speaker: Alviss
steps.text: I'm waiting for my shift. I'm supposed to be digging once the others have finished.

steps.speaker: Alviss
steps.text: I don't like the sound of these monsters, though.

steps.player: Monsters?

steps.speaker: Alviss
steps.text: I heard that Donal went exploring in the caves, and saw a huge monster.

steps.speaker: Alviss
steps.text: If you want to know more about it, ask Thorodin - he's working on the excavation right now.

options.text: Good day.
What are you doing down here?

steps.player: What are you doing down here?

steps.speaker: Fullangr
steps.text: I'm working on the digging, of course.

steps.speaker: Fullangr
steps.text: It's a small excavation, so only two of us can work on it at a time.

steps.speaker: Fullangr
steps.text: Thorodin and Donal were working on it earlier, but I hear Donal's run off to hide in the inn.

steps.player: Why is that?

steps.speaker: Fullangr
steps.text: Apparently he saw a monster when he was in the caves.

steps.speaker: Fullangr
steps.text: I'm not scared of monsters - I won't let them stop me from digging!

options.text: Good day.
What are you doing down here?

steps.player: What are you doing down here?

steps.speaker: Jari
steps.text: I'm waiting to work on the digging.

steps.speaker: Jari
steps.text: It's the first excavation I've worked on, and I'm looking forward to it.

steps.speaker: Jari
steps.text: I heard there were monsters in the other caves, though. I don't really want to meet them.

steps.player: Monsters?

steps.speaker: Jari
steps.text: Donal saw them when he explored the caves. He's been in the inn ever since.

options.text: Good day.
What are you doing down here?

steps.player: What are you doing down here?

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: We're extending the cave so more people can live in it.

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: These Miscellanians aren't so bad. They appreciate the benefits of living underground.

steps.player: ...such as?

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: You don't get rained on, for example.

steps.speaker: Thorodin

steps.player: Someone saw a monster?
Could you tell me more? The King asked me to investigate.

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: One of the other dwarves who was working with us saw it. His name's Donal.

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: He went further into the caves to plan our excavations, and a while later he came out shaking.

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: He's been in the inn ever since.

options.text: Good day.

steps.player: Good day.

options.text: What are you doing down here?

steps.player: What are you doing down here?

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: We're extending the cave so more people can live in it.

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: These Miscellanians aren't so bad. They appreciate the benefits of living underground.

steps.player: ...such as?

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: You don't get rained on, for example.

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: Have you spoken to Donal?

steps.player: Not yet, no.

steps.speaker: Thorodin
steps.text: Well, if you want to hear stories about monsters, he's the best one to ask.

options.text: Good day.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.player: What are you doing down in these caves?

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.speaker: Donal
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.text: I'm waiting to work on the excavations...

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.speaker: Donal
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.text: ...though I don't really want to start digging again.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.player: Why not? I thought digging was something dwarves were good at.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.speaker: Donal
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.text: Not with monsters like that one in those caves.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.speaker: Donal
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.text: It had huge teeth and flaming red eyes, and was almost the size of the tunnel!

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.speaker: Donal
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.text: Are you an adventurer, by any chance?

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.speaker: Donal
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.text: In that case, could you go and deal with that monster?

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.speaker: Donal
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.text: I don't want to have to face it again if it attacks the town.

options.text: Of course. Dealing with monsters is what I do best!

steps.player: Of course. Dealing with monsters is what I do best!

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: You'll need to get into the other caves first, of course.

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: There's a crack in the wall where the others are digging, but the rocks are loose, and can fall on you if you're not careful.

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: I can give you a mining prop to keep them from falling, if you give me a minute to find it...

steps.player: Okay, so all I have to do is get through that wall?

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: No, after that the only way you can get further is climbing up onto a high ledge, then crawling through a tunnel.

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: But the walls are slippery...

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: ...and I think I might have broken the lift when I fell off it on my way back.

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: You'll probably need to fix the lift - I doubt you'd be able to climb.

steps.player: And the monster's behind that tunnel?

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: Somewhere behind it. I couldn't get very far, what with the flooding in the tunnel.

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: There's some rope and some planks near the broken lift - those would probably come in handy.

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: Ah, here's that mining prop. I knew I had it somewhere.

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: Here you go. Good luck with fighting that monster.
mining prop

options.text: Why bother? It can't get through solid rock.

steps.player: Why bother? It can't get through solid rock.

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: That's what I thought, until I saw the sheer size of it. This thing probably MADE the tunnels!

steps.player: And you're sending me in to deal with it alone?

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: I've heard stories from the Miscellanians. If you're the Regent, you must be quite a strong hero.

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: So what are you worried about? You probably eat monsters like that for breakfast!

steps.player: I wouldn't put it quite like that...
But I'll help you after all. Now, how do I find this monster?

steps.text: Continues above at "You'll need to get into the other caves first, of course."

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.player: Just wondering if you were still here.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.speaker: Donal
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.text: I'm not going near that crack in the wall again.

to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.speaker: Donal
to-the-dungeon-with-you-talking-to-donal.text: Rock falls and so on are fine, but sea monsters in caves - never!
If the player lost the mining prop:

steps.player: I've lost that mining prop you gave me...

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: Lucky I have a spare, isn't it?

steps.speaker: Donal
steps.text: Here you go. Good luck with fighting that monster.

the-burnt-diary-getting-hit-by-rocks.text: Rocks tumble from the cave walls as you walk under them!

You add them to the diary you have.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: What do we do now?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: If you hadn't got drunk in that inn, Signy, we could have stayed there for longer.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Signy
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: It wasn't just me who got drunk. You looked like you were about to puke all over the barmaid.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Hild
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Reinn threw up anyway.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Reinn
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: I can't help it, I just have a weak stomach.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Reinn
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: You're no better, Hild. You said you knew where we were, and now look at us!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Reinn
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: We're cold, we're hungry and now we're LOST!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Hild
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: We wouldn't have been so cold if Armod had more diary pages he'd let us use!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Hey! I have to write down what's happened.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Otherwise father won't believe me when I tell him.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Signy
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: If your father listened to what you say, we wouldn't BE here.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Signy
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: We'd have passed the trials and we'd be proper adults!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Reinn
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Besides, it's not like he'll even look at the rubbish you've written in your diary.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: If only my father would come and save us.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Hild
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: If only SOMEONE would come and save us.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Someone's coming!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Signy
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Quick, let's hide!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: What if it's the monster again? What if it's one of the townspeople?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: What if my father's found out what we've been doing?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: H-hey! Where am I going to hide?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Hild
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Shhhh! Just pretend you're part of the scenery, or something!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Reinn
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: You're almost smart enough to make a good rock.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: You want me to hit you?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Signy
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Just act normal, Armod! And hurry!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: O-okay.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Don't bother me!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: I said, don't bother me!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: I'm being a rock at the moment.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.player: You can't be a rock. I heard you talking to people earlier.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: What did you hear?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.player: Your name's Armod, isn't it? I found your diary.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: What? How did you get it? Give it back!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.player: Not until you tell me what's going on.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Why should I tell you? We're going to do really well and show my father that we're true adults!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: What the-

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Did you read my diary?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: What are you even doing in these caves anyway? Everyone else was scared to come down here.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.player: Well, I'm the Regent of Miscellania. The King asked me to take a look-

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: You're the REGENT?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Um, you four, I think you'd better come out now. We're in big trouble.
Cutscene ends.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Reinn
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Nice impression of a rock you did there, Armod.

steps.text: So you're the adventurer we heard about, then. The one who gained the trust of the [prince/princess].

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.player: And you five are the people mentioned in Armod's diary, right?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Beigarth
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Armod, you should have burnt it all.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.player: Did you steal those goods from the Etceterians and the Miscellanians?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: It was Beigarth's idea, not mine!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: He said that if we disguised ourselves as soldiers, we could convince both the King and Queen that they were under attack. And it almost worked, too.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Reinn
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: It would have worked, if it hadn't been for that huge snake!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Reinn
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: We put the things we'd taken somewhere safe, so we could get them back when we made peace again.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Reinn
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Everything was going well, until we got back to that place, and a giant sea snake had moved in!

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Reinn
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: It's made a nest out of all the boxes and barrels.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: I don't care about the plan. If you can get rid of that sea snake, we'll be really grateful to you.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: We can't even get out of these dungeons while it's there.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Hild
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: I agree with him. I want to go back home.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Hild
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: It's cold here, we've got no food, and we can't go back to the town.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Signy
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Not after we got drunk and then didn't pay our bill.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: So, will you get rid of that sea snake?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.player: Of course. I was going to do that anyway.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Thank you so much. You've saved us from the brink of death.

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: Could I ask you for one more thing?

those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.speaker: Armod
those-meddling-kids-squeezing-through-th.text: PLEASE don't tell my father how badly we messed up.

those-meddling-kids-upon-killing-the-gia.text: A box of Etceterian items tumbles from the sea snake's nest.

those-meddling-kids-leaving-the-giant-se.speaker: Guard
those-meddling-kids-leaving-the-giant-se.text: Hello down there! Are you all right?

those-meddling-kids-leaving-the-giant-se.speaker: Guard
those-meddling-kids-leaving-the-giant-se.text: I'm up here, above this hole.

those-meddling-kids-leaving-the-giant-se.speaker: Guard
those-meddling-kids-leaving-the-giant-se.text: I've thrown down a rope - you sounded like you were trapped in there.

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-the-guard.text: If you still have the heavy box:

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: I'm surprised you managed to get out of there without breaking any bones.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Still, I can't let you go back down there until the Queen says it's safe.

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-the-guard.text: If you lost the heavy box:

steps.player: I don't suppose you've seen a large box around here, have you?

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Oh, so this is yours? You must have dropped it around here.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Seems rather heavy. Take better care of it this time.

those-meddling-kids-trying-to-go-back-in.speaker: Guard
those-meddling-kids-trying-to-go-back-in.text: Wait a minute! You can't go down there.

those-meddling-kids-trying-to-go-back-in.player: Why not? I came up through that hole...

those-meddling-kids-trying-to-go-back-in.speaker: Guard
those-meddling-kids-trying-to-go-back-in.text: Yes, and I'm surprised you managed to get out of there without breaking any bones.

those-meddling-kids-trying-to-go-back-in.speaker: Guard
those-meddling-kids-trying-to-go-back-in.text: Still, I can't let you go back down there until the Queen says it's safe.

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.player: I've talked to the Miscellanian citizens as well as the Etceterians.
The Etceterian citizens said that Miscellanian soldiers came to their houses and demanded tribute...

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.speaker: Queen Sigrid
those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.text: Just as I suspected! Vargas, you treacherous snake!

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.player: ...and the Miscellanian citizens said that the Etceterian army marched into their fields and demanded tithes!

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.speaker: Queen Sigrid
those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.text: Now I see his plan! Vargas isn't content with simply arguing; he wants to start a war even if it means swindling his own citizens!

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.speaker: Queen Sigrid
those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.text: Etceterian army? There hasn't been one for centuries! These Miscellanian soldiers of his must have disguised themselves.

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.speaker: Queen Sigrid
those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.text: If he wants an Etceterian army, then we'll have to raise one!

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.player: I've found out what caused all these problems.
A group of teenagers from Rellekka came to Etceteria to prove themselves as adults.
They said they tried to start a war, which they'd then stop, and be hailed as peacemakers.
They were the ones who disguised themselves as soldiers!

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.speaker: Queen Sigrid
those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.text: That explains what the citizens said about armies, I suppose.

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.speaker: Queen Sigrid
those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.text: But what about the items that went missing?

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.player: Well, there was a minor problem involving a sea snake...
But I dealt with it, and got the items back.

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.speaker: Queen Sigrid
those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.text: Finally, a ruler of Miscellania who's willing to do something for his neighbours.

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.speaker: Queen Sigrid
those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.text: Do you have the items with you?
If you lost the heavy box:

steps.player: ...I must have dropped the box on my way out of the dungeons.

steps.speaker: Queen Sigrid
steps.text: sigh* Well, if you ask the guard at the entrance to the dungeon, he might have picked it up.

steps.speaker: Queen Sigrid
steps.text: Of course, he won't know what it's for, so you'd better bring it back here once you find it.

steps.player: I shall do, your Majesty.

those-meddling-kids-talking-to-queen-sig.text: If you still have the heavy box:

steps.player: Yes, I have them here.

steps.speaker: Queen Sigrid
steps.text: Thank you, [Fremennik name]. You've shown yourself to be an excellent diplomat and warrior - not a combination that comes naturally to many.

steps.speaker: Queen Sigrid
steps.text: My citizens would like their items back, of course. One of my guards will deal with the items for you, and you will be provided with a suitable reward.

steps.speaker: Queen Sigrid
steps.text: Finally... I have a letter that I would like you to give to Vargas. This war was a mistake, and I've made a formal apology.

steps.player: I'll make sure to give it to him, your Majesty.

steps.speaker: Queen Sigrid
steps.text: Thank you for all your help, [Fremennik name]. To show our gratitude, the woodcutters and other workers of Etceteria have pledged to add a proportion of what they produce to your treasury.

steps.speaker: Queen Sigrid
steps.text: Now that you've finished giving these items back, please give my letter to Vargas.

steps.player: I'm afraid I've lost it.

steps.speaker: Queen Sigrid
steps.text: Very well, I'll write another. Try to take better care of this one.

at-peace-once-again-reading-the-letter-q.player: I'm not sure I should be reading this...

options.text: I shouldn't read other people's letters.

steps.player: I won't read that letter. It's for the King, not for me.
I'm not sure I should be reading this...

options.text: Go ahead and read it anyway.

steps.player: Oh, why not. I'm the Regent, after all.

at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.speaker: King Vargas
at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.text: How are your investigations going, [Fremennik name]?

at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.player: I've found the people who took the goods from your citizens!
They weren't Etceterian soldiers after all.
They were teenagers from Rellekka who were trying to prove themselves as adults, by starting a war and then bringing about peace.

at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.speaker: King Vargas
at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.text: Why didn't they just go through the trials as usual?

at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.speaker: King Vargas
at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.text: Unless they're the ones that the Council warned me about.

at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.speaker: King Vargas
at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.text: Still, I can't believe they'd start a war between Miscellania and Etceteria, just to show they were adults...

at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.speaker: King Vargas
at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.text: But at least you've found the missing goods. Do you have them with you?

at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.player: I'm afraid not, your Majesty. There were far too many for me to carry.

at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.speaker: King Vargas
at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.text: We'll have to send people down to collect them later, then.

at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.player: And I also spoke to Queen Sigrid of Etceteria.
She gave me a letter for you, which she said was a formal apology.

at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.speaker: King Vargas
at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.text: Oh? Do you have this letter with you?

steps.player: Er, I had it, but I seem to have lost it.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: You'd better ask Sigrid to write you another one, then.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: I'd like to see what she has to say.

at-peace-once-again-returning-to-king-va.text: If you still have the letter:

steps.player: Of course, your Majesty. Here you are.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: Let me see...

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: You defeated that sea snake? Sigrid seems rather impressed with that.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: And the caverns underneath her palace are joined to ours, I see.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: She thinks we should join forces to develop them for more houses.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: Finally... hmm. That's not what I'd have expected from Sigrid.

steps.player: What is it, your Majesty?

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: She, erm, says if I weren't a yeti, she might want to get to know me better.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: Since we're both warmongering fools, she thinks we'd get on well.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: I suppose she has a point there.

steps.player: Brand's suggestion worked, and I didn't even do anything.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: What was that?

steps.player: Nothing, your Majesty.
Do you want me to give a reply to Queen Sigrid?

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: No, no. I'll think about it for a while.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: Though I'd like to tell her I'm sorry for calling her a warmongering harpy.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: In the meantime, [Fremennik name], you have managed to avert a war and bring the culprits to light.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: The kingdom of Miscellania will have to reward you for this.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: I hear that the Etceterians are also grateful for your help, and have pledged some of their resources.

steps.speaker: King Vargas
steps.text: You can talk to Ghrim to deal with those, just as before.
Congratulations! Quest complete!

post-quest-talking-to-king-vargas.speaker: King Vargas
post-quest-talking-to-king-vargas.text: Thank you for your work in bringing peace back to these islands, [Fremennik name].

post-quest-talking-to-king-vargas.speaker: King Vargas
post-quest-talking-to-king-vargas.text: I hear that the Etceterians have also pledged to give you some of their resources, as thanks for preventing war once again.

post-quest-talking-to-king-vargas.speaker: King Vargas
post-quest-talking-to-king-vargas.text: Remember, speak to Ghrim if you require assistance.

steps.text: (Continues with Changing heirs dialogue.)

post-quest-talking-to-prince-brand.speaker: Prince Brand
post-quest-talking-to-prince-brand.text: I hear you made peace between our kingdom and Etceteria once more. Well done, [dear/[Fremennik name]].

post-quest-talking-to-princess-astrid.speaker: Princess Astrid
post-quest-talking-to-princess-astrid.text: I hear you made peace between our kingdom and Etceteria once more. Well done, [dear/[Fremennik name]].

post-quest-talking-to-queen-sigrid.speaker: Queen Sigrid
post-quest-talking-to-queen-sigrid.text: Thank you for all your help, [Fremennik name]. It's good to know that the Regent of Miscellania is willing to help his neighbours.
